question: In 2022, Eurostat introduced a statistical change that was adopted by Statistics Finland. As a result, interest subsidy loans used to develop affordable state-subsidised housing are now considered government debt under the EU’s fiscal governance framework. This change has caused the Finnish debt-to-GDP ratio to increase by several percentage points.

However, the Finnish Housing Finance and Development Centre (ARA) – whose functions have since been taken over by the Finnish Ministry of the Environment – has only acted as a guarantor for the loans. Financial institutions, such as banks, often grant the loans. This statistical modification threatens to curtail the construction of affordable housing in Finland.

Furthermore, it artificially increases the country’s debt-to-GDP ratio. Under the new EU fiscal framework, this could force the government to adopt additional restrictive fiscal measures amid stagnant growth and high unemployment. What will the Commission do to correct the misclassification and ensure that state guarantees aimed at supporting affordable housing are not considered government debt?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.3.2026) In 2022, Statistics Finland revised the statistical treatment of the interest subsidy loans granted by the Finnish Housing Finance and Development Centre (ARA). This revision did not apply to the separate loan guarantee scheme administered by ARA under the Act on State Guarantees for Rental Housing Loans (856/2008).
As a result, these State Guarantees are not included in Finland’s Maastricht debt. They are reported separately for information, as contingent liabilities not impacting debt.

The revision was agreed with the Statistical Office of the European Union, which confirmed that the statistical recording complies with the rules on sector classification under the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010) and the Manual on Government Deficit and Debt.
